quests.instruction: Read the announcement and find the actual salary adjustment percentage, not the software change.
quests.passage: Dual Announcement: Starting next quarter, all full-time employees will receive a 3.5 percent salary adjustment to account for cost of living. Separately, the company is also updating its expense reporting software, which will require all receipts to be submitted digitally going forward.
quests.hint: Separate the two unrelated topics in the announcement and find the one this question asks about.
quests.explanation: The salary adjustment is 3.5 percent; the software change is a separate, unrelated update.

quests.instruction: Read the excerpt and find the fee charged per trade, not the annual management fee.
quests.passage: Investment Prospectus Excerpt: The fund charges a 0.75 percent annual management fee. A separate transaction fee of $15 applies to each trade made within the account, regardless of trade size.
quests.hint: Judge which fee applies per trade, not annually.
quests.explanation: The transaction fee is $15 per trade; 0.75 percent is the separate annual management fee.

quests.instruction: Read the summary and find the move-in fee, not the application fee.
quests.passage: Lease Fee Summary: The application fee is $50 and is non-refundable regardless of approval status. A separate move-in fee of $200 is charged only to approved applicants and is due before keys are issued.
quests.hint: Judge which fee is the move-in fee, not the application fee.
quests.explanation: The move-in fee is $200; $50 is the separate, non-refundable application fee.

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find the benefit that comes only with the VIP pass.
quests.passage: Conference Pass Comparison: The standard pass includes access to all breakout sessions and the exhibit hall. The VIP pass includes everything in the standard pass plus a reserved seat at the keynote and a private networking dinner.
quests.hint: Judge which benefit is exclusive to VIP, not shared with standard.
quests.explanation: The private networking dinner is VIP-only; breakout sessions and the exhibit hall are included in both passes.

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find the gold plan's deductible, not the bronze plan's.
quests.passage: Health Plan Comparison: The bronze plan has a lower monthly premium but a higher annual deductible of $4,500. The gold plan has a higher premium but a lower deductible of $1,200, making it better suited for frequent medical care.
quests.hint: Judge which deductible belongs to the gold plan, not the bronze plan.
quests.explanation: The gold plan's deductible is $1,200; $4,500 belongs to the bronze plan instead.

quests.instruction: Read the letter and find the grant amount, not the loan amount.
quests.passage: Financial Aid Letter: Your need-based grant award for this year totals $6,200 and does not need to be repaid. You have also been offered a subsidized loan of $3,500, which begins accruing interest after graduation.
quests.hint: Judge which figure is the grant, not the loan.
quests.explanation: The grant award is $6,200 and doesn't need repayment; $3,500 is the separate loan offer.

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find how often the pro edition receives updates.
quests.passage: Product Version Comparison: The standard edition includes core features and receives updates twice a year. The pro edition includes all standard features plus advanced analytics tools, with updates released monthly instead of twice a year.
quests.hint: Judge which update frequency belongs to the pro edition, not the standard edition.
quests.explanation: The pro edition updates monthly; twice a year is the standard edition's slower update schedule.
quests.targetInfo: Update frequency for the pro edition

quests.instruction: Read the tiers and find the benefit exclusive to Gold status.
quests.passage: Airline Status Tiers: Silver status requires 25,000 miles annually and includes priority boarding. Gold status requires 50,000 miles annually and includes priority boarding plus two free checked bags per flight.
quests.hint: Judge which benefit is exclusive to Gold, not shared with Silver.
quests.explanation: Two free checked bags is Gold-exclusive; priority boarding is included in both tiers.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find what outlet locations actually carry, not the flagship store.
quests.passage: Retail Store Notice: Our flagship location carries the full product catalog and offers personal styling appointments. Our outlet locations carry a limited selection of past-season items at discounted prices, without styling services.
quests.hint: Judge which items belong to outlet locations, not the flagship store.
quests.explanation: Outlets carry past-season items; the full catalog and styling appointments are flagship-only.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the deadline for beneficiaries, not creditors.
quests.passage: Legal Notice: Creditors must file claims against the estate within ninety days of this notice's publication. Beneficiaries wishing to contest the will have a separate deadline of six months from the date of probate filing.
quests.hint: Judge which deadline applies to beneficiaries, not creditors.
quests.explanation: Beneficiaries have six months to contest the will; ninety days is the separate deadline for creditors.
quests.targetInfo: Deadline for beneficiaries to contest the will

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the length of extended coverage, not the standard warranty.
quests.passage: Warranty Notice: The manufacturer's warranty covers defects in materials for two years from purchase. Extended coverage, purchased separately, extends protection to five years but excludes cosmetic damage.
quests.hint: Judge which length belongs to extended coverage, not the standard warranty.
quests.explanation: Extended coverage lasts five years; two years is the standard, included warranty period.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the cost of a commercial permit, not a residential one.
quests.passage: City Notice: Residential parking permits cost $35 annually and allow parking in designated residential zones only. Commercial parking permits cost $120 annually and allow parking in both residential and commercial zones.
quests.hint: Judge which cost belongs to commercial permits, not residential ones.
quests.explanation: Commercial permits cost $120; $35 is the separate residential permit price.
quests.targetInfo: Cost of a commercial parking permit

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the cost of the annual plan, not the monthly plan.
quests.passage: Subscription Box Notice: The monthly plan costs $34.99 and can be canceled anytime without penalty. The annual plan costs $299.99, which works out to a lower monthly rate but requires a full year's commitment.
quests.hint: Judge which price belongs to the annual plan, not the monthly plan.
quests.explanation: The annual plan costs $299.99; $34.99 is the separate monthly price.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the cost of apartment-style housing, not the traditional dorm.
quests.passage: University Housing Notice: Traditional dorm rooms cost $4,800 per semester and include a meal plan. Apartment-style housing costs $6,400 per semester and does not include a meal plan, though a kitchen is provided instead.
quests.hint: Judge which cost belongs to apartment-style housing, not the traditional dorm.
quests.explanation: Apartment-style housing costs $6,400; $4,800 is the separate traditional dorm price.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the feature that comes only with the unlimited plan.
quests.passage: Wireless Plan Notice: The basic plan includes 10GB of data for $40 monthly. The unlimited plan costs $65 monthly and includes unlimited data along with mobile hotspot access.
quests.hint: Judge which feature is exclusive to the unlimited plan.
quests.explanation: Mobile hotspot access is exclusive to the unlimited plan; 10GB and $40 describe the basic plan.
quests.targetInfo: Feature exclusive to the unlimited plan

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find the SUV's daily rate, not the economy car's.
quests.passage: Car Rental Comparison: The economy car rents for $32 per day and seats up to four passengers. The SUV rents for $58 per day and seats up to seven passengers, making it a better fit for larger groups.
quests.hint: Judge which rate belongs to the SUV, not the economy car.
quests.explanation: The SUV rents for $58 per day; $32 is the separate economy car rate.

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find what the premium package adds beyond the basic package.
quests.passage: Wedding Package Comparison: The basic package includes venue rental and basic catering for $8,000. The premium package includes everything in the basic package plus photography and a live band, for $14,500.
quests.hint: Judge which items are added by the premium package specifically.
quests.explanation: The premium package adds photography and a live band; venue rental and catering are in both packages.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the cost of full-time enrollment, not part-time.
quests.passage: Childcare Program Notice: Part-time enrollment covers three days per week at $650 monthly. Full-time enrollment covers five days per week at $980 monthly, including all meals and snacks.
quests.hint: Judge which cost belongs to full-time enrollment, not part-time.
quests.explanation: Full-time enrollment costs $980; $650 is the separate part-time price.

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find the feature included only with the larger suite.
quests.passage: Office Lease Comparison: The smaller suite is 1,200 square feet at $2,400 monthly. The larger suite is 2,000 square feet at $3,600 monthly and includes a private conference room.
quests.hint: Judge which feature is exclusive to the larger suite.
quests.explanation: The private conference room is exclusive to the larger suite; the smaller suite doesn't include it.
quests.targetInfo: Feature included only with the larger suite

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find the premium card's cash back rate on groceries and gas.
quests.passage: Credit Card Comparison: The standard card has no annual fee and offers 1 percent cash back on all purchases. The premium card has a $95 annual fee but offers 3 percent cash back on groceries and gas.
quests.hint: Judge which cash back rate belongs to the premium card, not the standard card.
quests.explanation: The premium card offers 3 percent on groceries and gas; 1 percent is the standard card's general rate.
quests.targetInfo: Cash back rate on groceries and gas with the premium card

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find everything included in the full-service option.
quests.passage: Moving Service Comparison: The basic service includes loading and transport only, for $600. The full-service option includes packing, loading, transport, and unpacking, for $1,450.
quests.hint: Judge which list of services belongs to the full-service option.
quests.explanation: Full-service includes packing, loading, transport, and unpacking; the basic service covers loading and transport only.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the cost of toddler care, not infant care.
quests.passage: Daycare Fee Notice: Infant care costs $1,400 monthly due to a lower staff-to-child ratio required by regulation. Toddler care costs $1,100 monthly, reflecting the less intensive staffing requirement.
quests.hint: Judge which cost belongs to toddler care, not infant care.
quests.explanation: Toddler care costs $1,100; $1,400 is the separate, higher infant care price.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the feature exclusive to luxury boarding.
quests.passage: Pet Boarding Rate Notice: Standard boarding costs $45 per night and includes two walks daily. Luxury boarding costs $75 per night and includes four walks daily plus a private suite instead of a shared kennel.
quests.hint: Judge which feature is exclusive to luxury boarding.
quests.explanation: The private suite is exclusive to luxury boarding; standard boarding uses a shared kennel instead.

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find the cost of the full-access pass, not the weekday pass.
quests.passage: Ski Pass Comparison: The weekday pass costs $89 and is valid Monday through Friday only. The full-access pass costs $149 and is valid every day, including weekends and holidays.
quests.hint: Judge which cost belongs to the full-access pass, not the weekday pass.
quests.explanation: The full-access pass costs $149; $89 is the separate, weekday-only price.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find what full-value protection actually covers.
quests.passage: Moving Insurance Notice: Basic released-value protection is included at no cost but covers only 60 cents per pound per item. Full-value protection can be purchased separately and covers the item's full replacement cost.
quests.hint: Judge which coverage level applies to full-value protection, not the basic default.
quests.explanation: Full-value protection covers full replacement cost; the free default only covers 60 cents per pound.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the cost of the full-day program, not the half-day program.
quests.passage: Summer Camp Fee Notice: The half-day program costs $220 per week and runs from 9 to 1. The full-day program costs $380 per week and runs from 8 to 5, including lunch and an afternoon snack.
quests.hint: Judge which cost belongs to the full-day program, not the half-day program.
quests.explanation: The full-day program costs $380; $220 is the separate half-day price.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the enterprise tier's response time, not the basic tier's.
quests.passage: Software Support Tier Notice: The basic support tier includes email support with a 48-hour response time. The enterprise tier includes phone support with a guaranteed 2-hour response time, available 24/7.
quests.hint: Judge which response time belongs to the enterprise tier, not the basic tier.
quests.explanation: The enterprise tier guarantees a 2-hour response; 48 hours is the basic tier's slower response time.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find the maximum bonus for senior-level employees, not associate-level.
quests.passage: Corporate Bonus Structure Notice: Employees at the associate level are eligible for a bonus of up to 8 percent of base salary, contingent on individual performance reviews. Employees at the senior level are eligible for up to 15 percent, contingent on both individual and team performance.
quests.hint: Judge which bonus percentage belongs to senior-level employees, not associate-level.
quests.explanation: Senior-level employees can earn up to 15 percent; 8 percent is the separate, lower associate-level cap.
quests.targetInfo: Maximum bonus percentage for senior-level employees

quests.instruction: Read the comparison and find the cost of the park-hopper ticket, not the single-day ticket.
quests.passage: Theme Park Ticket Comparison: The single-day ticket costs $89 and grants access to one park only. The park-hopper ticket costs $135 and allows unlimited movement between all parks on the same day.
quests.hint: Judge which cost belongs to the park-hopper ticket, not the single-day ticket.
quests.explanation: The park-hopper ticket costs $135; $89 is the separate, single-park price.

quests.instruction: Read the notice and find what happens to premium plan users who go over their data allowance.
quests.passage: Data Plan Overage Notice: Customers on the standard plan are charged $10 per additional gigabyte after exceeding their monthly allowance. Customers on the premium plan instead have overage automatically throttled to slower speeds at no extra charge.
quests.hint: Judge which consequence applies to premium plan users, not standard plan users.
quests.explanation: Premium users are throttled to slower speeds; standard plan users instead pay $10 per extra gigabyte.
quests.targetInfo: What happens to premium plan users who exceed their allowance
